outcome_scope: 2026 DOI10.3389/fvets.2025.1693838; 20 dogs with osteoarthritis randomized to 90 days oral multi-ingredient Asudyn versus mavacoxib; product includes 3 mg standardized Piper nigrum extract per tablet plus turmeric, fish oil and others. Canine pain VAS and CBPI reported; authors describe improvement in both arms; no isolated pepper or human Parkinson contrast. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12927037/

2026 DOI10.3390/nu18020223; 30 adults with chronic pain randomized crossover turmeric with 300 mg ground black pepper versus same turmeric alone. No statistically significant pepper contrast p=0.157; not equivalence and no no-turmeric control. Previously assessed. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12844896/

2024 DOI10.1016/j.jep.2024.117833; rheumatoid arthritis trial 70 randomized, 50 per-protocol; oral Qurs-e-Mafasil contains Piper nigrum, ginger, colchicum and ashwagandha versus celecoxib. Final pain VAS mean difference 3.00, 95% CI -1.82 to 7.84, p=0.219; uncertainty does not establish equivalence. Full trial tables/supplement remain access-limited; no isolated pepper. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38316221/

2020 DOI10.1002/ptr.6671; 60 knee osteoarthritis patients, oral turmeric extract plus black pepper and ginger versus naproxen for four weeks. Abstract reports PGE2 biomarker but no numerical clinical pain comparison; full outcome table remains a possible access gap. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32180294/

2014 DOI10.1089/acm.2013.0453; 60 with neck pain, topical cream containing black pepper plus marjoram, lavender and peppermint oils versus unscented cream for four weeks. Both arms improved pain VAS within group; no isolated ingested pepper comparison; full pain contrast tables remain to verify. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25192562/

2014 DOI10.1016/j.ctim.2013.08.014; 30 healthy volunteers within-person comparison of topical Trikatu containing dried Piper nigrum and P. retrofractum fruits and ginger versus camphor/menthol/eucalyptus. No significant differences in assessed pain or other symptoms at measured times; not a placebo noninferiority test or oral culinary pepper. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24559814/

2015 online DOI10.1517/13543776.2016.1118057; patent/derivative review covering piperine and analogues with references to Parkinson and pain targets, not an original clinical dietary pepper comparison. Complete review bibliography remains unverified. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26560940/
